verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
Until the day when He was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, He had given commandments to the apostles whom He had chosen.
After His passion (suffering and death), He showed Himself alive to them by many infallible proofs (sure signs). They saw Him for 40 days, and He spoke about the things of the kingdom of God.
When He was gathered together with them, He commanded them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father. He said: You have heard about this from Me.
For John truly baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.
So when they had come together, they asked Him: Lord, will You at this time restore (give back) the kingdom to Israel?
He said to them: It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father has put in His own power.
But you will receive power after the Holy Spirit has come upon you. And you will be witnesses unto Me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and to the farthest part of the earth.
When He had spoken these things, while they watched, He was taken up. And a cloud received Him out of their sight.
While they looked steadfastly (kept staring) toward heaven as He went up, two men stood by them in white clothes.
They said: Men of Galilee, why do you stand gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus, who is taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you have seen Him go into heaven.
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet (the Mount of Olives), which is a sabbath day's journey (a short walk, about 1 mile) from Jerusalem.

When they came in, they went up into an upper room. Staying there were Peter, James, John, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon Zelotes (the Zealot), and Judas the brother of James.
These all continued with one accord (all agreeing together) in prayer and supplication (asking God), with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
In those days Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples and spoke. The number of people together was about 120.
Men and brothers, this scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke before by the mouth of David about Judas, who was the guide for those who took (arrested) Jesus.
For he was numbered (counted) with us, and had a part in this ministry (work).
Now this man bought a field with the reward of iniquity (money paid for his sin). And falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his bowels (insides) gushed out.
This was known to all the people living at Jerusalem. So that field is called in their own language Aceldama, which means The field of blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms: Let his home be desolate (empty), and let no man live in it. And: Let another take his bishoprick (his office).
So, of these men who have been with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
Beginning from the baptism of John to that same day when He was taken up from us, one must be ordained (chosen) to be a witness with us of His resurrection (rising from the dead).
They appointed (put forward) 2 men: Joseph called Barsabas, who was also named Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed and said: You, Lord, who know the hearts of all men, show which of these 2 You have chosen,
To take the part of this ministry (work) and apostleship, from which Judas fell by transgression (sin), so that he might go to his own place.
Then they cast their lots (a way of choosing), and the lot fell on Matthias. And he was numbered (counted) with the 11 apostles.

verses.text: When the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all with one accord (all agreeing together) in one place.
Suddenly there came a sound from heaven like a rushing, mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
There appeared to them tongues split apart, like fire, and it sat upon each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other tongues (languages), as the Spirit gave them the words to say.
There were living at Jerusalem Jews, devout (God-fearing) men, out of every nation under heaven.
When this was noised abroad (when people heard about it), the crowd came together and were confounded (confused), because every man heard them speak in his own language.
They were all amazed and marveled (wondered), saying to one another: Look, are not all these who speak from Galilee?
How then do we each hear them in our own language, the language we were born with?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people living in Mesopotamia, in Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome, Jews and proselytes (people who became Jews),
Cretes and Arabians, we hear them speak in our own languages the wonderful works of God.
They were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying to one another: What does this mean?
Others mocking said: These men are full of new wine.
But Peter, standing up with the 11, lifted up his voice and said to them: Men of Judea, and all you who live at Jerusalem, know this, and listen to my words.
For these men are not drunk, as you suppose (think), since it is only the third hour of the day (9 in the morning).
But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:

And it will come to pass in the last days, says God, I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh (all people). Your sons and your daughters will prophesy (speak God's message), your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
And on My servants and on My handmaidens (women servants) I will pour out My Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy (speak God's message).
I will show wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth below: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable (glorious) day of the Lord comes.
And it will come to pass that whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth was a man approved (shown to be true) by God among you by miracles, wonders, and signs, which God did by Him in the middle of you, as you yourselves also know.
Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel (set plan) and foreknowledge of God, you have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and killed.
God raised Him up, having loosed (freed Him from) the pains of death, because it was not possible that He should be held by it.
For David speaks about Him: I saw the Lord always before my face. For He is at my right hand, so that I should not be moved.
So my heart rejoiced, and my tongue was glad. Also my flesh (body) will rest in hope,
Because You will not leave my soul in hell (the grave), and You will not let Your Holy One see corruption (decay).
You have made known to me the ways of life. You will make me full of joy with Your presence.
Men and brothers, let me speak freely to you about the patriarch (father of the nation) David. He is both dead and buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
So being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that from the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, He would raise up Christ to sit on his throne,
David, seeing this before, spoke about the resurrection (rising from the dead) of Christ, that His soul was not left in hell (the grave), and His flesh (body) did not see corruption (decay).
This Jesus God has raised up, and we are all witnesses of it.
So being lifted up by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has poured out this, which you now see and hear.
For David has not gone up into the heavens. But he says himself: The LORD said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand,
Until I make Your enemies Your footstool.
So let all the house of Israel know for sure that God has made that same Jesus, whom you have crucified, both Lord and Christ.
When they heard this, they were pricked (deeply hurt) in their heart, and said to Peter and to the rest of the apostles: Men and brothers, what shall we do?

Then Peter said to them: Repent (turn from your sin), and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ because of the remission (forgiveness) of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God will call.
With many other words he testified (told the truth) and exhorted (urged) them, saying: Save yourselves from this untoward (crooked) generation.
Then those who gladly received his word were baptized. And the same day about 3,000 souls (people) were added to them.
They continued steadfastly (kept on faithfully) in the apostles' doctrine (teaching) and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
Fear came upon every soul (person), and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles.
All who believed were together, and had all things common (shared everything).
They sold their possessions and goods, and parted (gave) them to all men, as every man had need.
They continued daily with one accord (all agreeing together) in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house. They ate their food with gladness and singleness (sincerity) of heart,
Praising God, and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily those who should be saved.

verses.text: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon).

A certain man who was lame from his mother's womb (from birth) was carried there. They laid him daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms (gifts of money) from those who went into the temple.
He saw Peter and John about to go into the temple, and asked for alms (a gift of money).
Peter, fastening his eyes on him with John, said: Look on us.
He gave heed (paid attention) to them, expecting to receive something from them.
Then Peter said: Silver and gold I have none, but what I have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk.
He took him by the right hand and lifted him up. And right away his feet and ankle bones received strength.
Leaping up, he stood and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They knew that it was he who sat for alms (gifts of money) at the Beautiful gate of the temple. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
As the lame man who was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the porch called Solomon's, greatly wondering.

When Peter saw it, he answered the people: Men of Israel, why do you marvel (wonder) at this? Or why do you look so earnestly (hard) at us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man walk?

The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Son Jesus, whom you delivered up, and denied Him in the presence of Pilate, when Pilate had decided to let Him go.
But you denied the Holy One and the Just (Righteous One), and asked for a murderer to be given to you,
And killed the Prince of life, whom God has raised from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
His name, through faith in His name, has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which is by Him has given him this perfect soundness (complete healing) in front of you all.
And now, brothers, I know that you did it through ignorance (not knowing), as your rulers also did.
But those things which God had shown before by the mouth of all His prophets, that Christ should suffer, He has fulfilled in this way.
So repent (turn from your sin), and be converted (turn to God), so that your sins may be blotted out (wiped away), when the times of refreshing will come from the presence of the Lord.
He will send Jesus Christ, who before was preached to you,
Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution (restoring) of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.
For Moses truly said to the fathers: A Prophet the Lord your God will raise up to you from your brothers, like me. You must hear Him in all things, whatever He says to you.
And it will come to pass that every soul (person) who will not hear that Prophet will be destroyed from among the people.
Yes, and all the prophets from Samuel and those who came after, as many as have spoken, have also told about these days.
You are the children of the prophets, and of the agreement which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham: And in your seed (family line) all the families of the earth will be blessed.
To you first God, having raised up His Son Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities (sins).

verses.text: As they spoke to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,
Being grieved (upset) that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection (rising) from the dead.
They laid hands on them, and put them in hold (jail) until the next day, for it was now evening.
But many of those who heard the word believed. And the number of the men was about 5,000.
On the next day, their rulers, elders, and scribes (teachers of the law),
And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and as many as were of the family of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.
When they had set them in the middle, they asked: By what power, or by what name, have you done this?
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: You rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
If we this day are examined about the good deed done to the weak man, by what means he is made whole (healed),

Be it known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by Him this man stands here in front of you whole (healed).
This is the stone which was set at nought (thrown away as worthless) by you builders, which has become the head of the corner (the most important stone).
Neither is there salvation in any other. For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and saw that they were unlearned and ignorant (not trained in schools) men, they marveled (wondered). And they took knowledge (noticed) that they had been with Jesus.
Seeing the man who was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they talked among themselves,
Saying: What shall we do to these men? For truly a notable (clear) miracle has been done by them, and it is plain to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us strictly threaten them, that from now on they speak to no man in this name.
They called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered them: Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you more than to God, you judge.
For we cannot help but speak the things which we have seen and heard.
So when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding nothing to punish them for, because of the people. For all men glorified God for what was done.
For the man on whom this miracle of healing was shown was more than 40 years old.
Being let go, they went to their own company (friends), and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
When they heard that, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord (all agreeing together), and said: Lord, You are God, who has made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that is in them.
You said by the mouth of Your servant David: Why did the heathen (nations) rage, and the people imagine vain (useless) things?
The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against His Christ.
For truly against Your holy child Jesus, whom You have anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) and the people of Israel, were gathered together,
To do whatever Your hand and Your counsel (plan) determined before to be done.
And now, Lord, look on their threatenings, and grant (give) to Your servants that with all boldness they may speak Your word,
By stretching out Your hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of Your holy child Jesus.
When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered together was shaken. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.
The crowd of those who believed were of one heart and of one soul. Not one of them said that any of the things he owned was his own, but they had all things common (shared everything).
With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection (rising from the dead) of the Lord Jesus. And great grace was upon them all.
There was no one among them who lacked (needed anything). For as many as owned lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,
And laid them down at the apostles' feet. And it was given to every man as he had need.
Joses, who was surnamed (also named) Barnabas by the apostles, which means The son of consolation (comfort), a Levite, and from the country of Cyprus,
Having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet.

verses.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession (some land).
Ananias kept back part of the price. His wife also knew about it. He brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet.
But Peter said: Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While it remained, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your own power? Why have you thought of this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God.
Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and gave up the ghost (died). And great fear came on all those who heard these things.
The young men got up, wound him up (wrapped his body), carried him out, and buried him.
About 3 hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter answered her: Tell me whether you sold the land for so much. She said: Yes, for so much.

Then Peter said to her: How is it that you have agreed together to tempt (test) the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.
Then right away Sapphira fell down at Peter's feet, and gave up the ghost (died). The young men came in and found her dead. They carried her out and buried her by her husband.
Great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.
By the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders done among the people. And they were all with one accord (all agreeing together) in Solomon's porch.
Of the rest, no man dared to join himself to them. But the people magnified (praised) them.
Believers were added to the Lord more and more, crowds of both men and women.
So they brought the sick out into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, so that at least the shadow of Peter passing by might fall on some of them.
Also a crowd came out of the cities around to Jerusalem. They brought sick people, and those who were vexed (troubled) with unclean spirits. And every one of them was healed.
Then the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, which is the sect (group) of the Sadducees. They were filled with indignation (anger),
And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.
But the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night, brought them out, and said:
Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

When they heard that, they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught. But the high priest came, and those who were with him. They called the council together, and all the senate (elders) of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have the apostles brought.
But when the officers came, and did not find the apostles in the prison, they went back and told,
Saying: The prison truly we found shut with all safety, and the keepers standing outside before the doors. But when we had opened, we found no man inside.
When the high priest, the captain of the temple, and the chief priests heard these things, they doubted (wondered) what this would grow into.
Then one came and told them, saying: Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people.
Then the captain went with the officers, and brought the apostles without violence. For they feared the people, that they might be stoned.
When they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest asked them,
Saying: Did we not strictly command you that you should not teach in this name? And look, you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine (teaching), and intend to bring this man's blood upon us.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said: We ought to obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed and hanged on a tree.
God has exalted (lifted up) Jesus with His right hand to be a Prince and a Savior, to give repentance (a change of heart) to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.
And we are His witnesses of these things. And so is also the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.
When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel (made plans) to kill the apostles.
Then a Pharisee in the council stood up, named Gamaliel, a doctor (teacher) of the law, who was honored among all the people. He commanded them to put the apostles outside for a little while.
Gamaliel said to them: Men of Israel, take heed (be careful) about what you plan to do with these men.

For before these days Theudas rose up, boasting himself to be somebody. A number of men, about 400, joined themselves to him. He was killed, and all who obeyed him were scattered, and brought to nothing.

After this man, Judas of Galilee rose up in the days of the taxing (the count of the people), and drew away much people after him. He also perished (died), and all, even as many as obeyed him, were scattered.
And now I say to you: Stay away from these men, and let them alone. For if this counsel (plan) or this work is of men, it will come to nothing.
But if it is of God, you cannot overthrow it. Or else you may be found even to fight against God.
They agreed with Gamaliel. When they had called the apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
Daily in the temple, and in every house, they did not stop teaching and preaching Jesus Christ.

verses.text: In those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied (growing), there arose a murmuring (complaining) of the Grecians (Greek-speaking Jews) against the Hebrews. They complained because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration (giving out of food).
Then the 12 called the crowd of the disciples to them, and said: It is not reason (not right) that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.
So, brothers, look among you for 7 men of honest report (good name), full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry (work) of the word.

This saying pleased the whole crowd. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte (a man who became a Jew) of Antioch.
They set these men before the apostles. When the apostles had prayed, they laid their hands on them.
The word of God increased. And the number of the disciples in Jerusalem multiplied (grew) greatly. And a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.

Then some from the synagogue (meeting house) arose, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines (freed slaves), and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and some of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing (arguing) with Stephen.
They were not able to resist (stand against) the wisdom and the Spirit by which Stephen spoke.
Then they secretly got men to say: We have heard him speak blasphemous words (words against God) against Moses, and against God.
They stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes (teachers of the law). They came upon Stephen, caught him, and brought him to the council.
They set up false witnesses, who said: This man does not stop speaking blasphemous words (words against God) against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Moses delivered (gave) to us.
All who sat in the council, looking steadfastly (staring) at Stephen, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.

verses.text: Then the high priest said: Are these things so?
Stephen said: Men, brothers, and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Charran (Haran).
God said to Abraham: Get out of your country, and from your family, and come into the land which I will show you.
Then Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, and lived in Charran (Haran). From there, when his father was dead, God moved him into this land, where you now live.

God gave Abraham no inheritance in it, no, not even enough to set his foot on. Yet God promised that He would give it to him for a possession, and to his seed (family line) after him, when as yet he had no child.
God spoke this way: That his seed (family line) should live as strangers in a foreign land. The people there would bring them into bondage (slavery), and treat them badly 400 years.
And the nation to whom they will be in bondage (slavery) I will judge, said God. After that they will come out, and serve Me in this place.

God gave Abraham the agreement of circumcision (cutting off the foreskin). So Abraham became the father of Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob. And Jacob became the father of the 12 patriarchs (fathers of the tribes).
The patriarchs (fathers of the tribes), moved with envy (jealousy), sold Joseph into Egypt. But God was with Joseph,
And delivered (rescued) Joseph out of all his afflictions (troubles). God gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh made Joseph governor over Egypt and all his house.
Now there came a dearth (famine) over all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction (trouble). Our fathers found no sustenance (food).
But when Jacob heard that there was corn (grain) in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.
At the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers. And Joseph's family was made known to Pharaoh.
Then Joseph sent and called his father Jacob to him, and all his family, 75 souls (people).
So Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he and our fathers,
And they were carried over into Sychem (Shechem), and laid in the sepulchre (tomb) that Abraham bought for a sum of money from the sons of Emmor (Hamor) the father of Sychem.
But when the time of the promise came near, which God had sworn (promised with an oath) to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
Until another king arose, who did not know Joseph.
This king dealt subtly (with tricks) with our family, and treated our fathers badly. He made them cast out (leave outside) their young children, so that the babies would not live.
In that time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair (very beautiful) to God. He was nourished (cared for) in his father's house 3 months.
When Moses was cast out (left outside), Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished (raised) him as her own son.
Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
When Moses was 40 years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
Seeing one of them suffer wrong, Moses defended him, and avenged (paid back) the one who was oppressed (treated cruelly), and struck the Egyptian.
For Moses supposed (thought) his brothers would have understood how God by his hand would deliver (rescue) them. But they did not understand.
The next day Moses showed himself to 2 of them as they fought. He would have set them at one (at peace) again, saying: Sirs, you are brothers. Why do you do wrong to one another?
But the one who did his neighbor wrong thrust Moses away, saying: Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Will you kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?
Then Moses fled at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian (Midian). There he became the father of 2 sons.
When 40 years were finished, there appeared to Moses in the wilderness (desert) of mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight. As he came near to look at it, the voice of the Lord came to him,
Saying: I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and dared not look.
Then the Lord said to him: Take off your shoes from your feet. For the place where you stand is holy ground.
I have seen, I have seen the affliction (suffering) of My people who are in Egypt. I have heard their groaning, and have come down to deliver (rescue) them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt.
This Moses whom they refused, saying: Who made you a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer (rescuer) by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
Moses brought them out, after he had shown wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness (desert) 40 years.
This is that Moses, who said to the children of Israel: A Prophet the Lord your God will raise up to you from your brothers, like me. Him you will hear.

This is Moses, who was in the church (gathering of God's people) in the wilderness (desert) with the angel who spoke to him in mount Sinai, and with our fathers. Moses received the lively oracles (living words of God) to give to us.
Our fathers would not obey Moses, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt.
They said to Aaron: Make us gods to go before us. For as for this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not (do not know) what has become of him.
They made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host (army) of heaven (the sun, moon, and stars), as it is written in the book of the prophets: O house of Israel, have you offered to Me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of 40 years in the wilderness (desert)?
Yes, you took up the tabernacle (tent) of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures (idols) which you made to worship them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.
Our fathers had the tabernacle (tent) of witness in the wilderness (desert), as God had appointed (ordered), speaking to Moses, that he should make it by the pattern that he had seen.
Our fathers who came after also brought it in with Jesus (Joshua) into the land of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, to the days of David.
David found favor before God, and desired to find a tabernacle (dwelling place) for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built God a house.
But the most High does not live in temples made with hands, as the prophet says:
Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What house will you build Me? says the Lord. Or what is the place of My rest?
Has not My hand made all these things?
You stiffnecked (stubborn) and uncircumcised (unclean) in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you.

Which of the prophets have your fathers not persecuted (attacked)? They have killed those who showed before about the coming of the Just One (the Righteous One). Of Him you have now been the betrayers and murderers.
You have received the law by the disposition (order) of angels, and have not kept it.
When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on Stephen with their teeth (ground their teeth at him).
But Stephen, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly (stared) into heaven. He saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God.
Stephen said: Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.
Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon Stephen with one accord (all together),
And cast him out of the city, and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man whose name was Saul.
They stoned Stephen, as he was calling upon God and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Stephen kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge (do not hold this sin against them). When he had said this, he fell asleep (died).

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Saul agreed that Stephen should be killed. That same day, a time of great trouble and attacks began against the church in Jerusalem. All the believers except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.
Faithful men buried Stephen and cried deeply for him.
But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off both men and women and put them in prison.
Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and told the people there about the Messiah.
When the crowds heard Philip and saw the signs he performed, they all paid close attention to what he said.
Evil spirits came out of many people, screaming loudly as they left. Many people who could not move or could not walk were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
Now for some time, a man named Simon had used magic tricks in the city, and he amazed all the people of Samaria. He bragged that he was someone great,
All the people, important and ordinary, paid attention to him and said: This man is rightly called the Great Power of God.
They followed him because he had amazed them for a long time with his magic tricks.
But Philip proclaimed the good news of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ. The people believed him. Both men and women were baptized.
Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip everywhere and was amazed by the great signs and miracles he saw.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
When they arrived, they prayed for the new believers there that they might receive the Holy Spirit,
Because the Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had simply been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given at the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money
And said: Give me also this ability so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.
Peter answered: May your money perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!
You have no part or share in this work, because your heart is not right before God.
Turn away from this evil, and pray to the Lord. Maybe He will forgive you for having such a thought in your heart.
For I see that you are full of bitterness, and sin has trapped you.
Then Simon answered: Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.
After Peter and John had preached the word of the Lord and told people about Jesus, they went back to Jerusalem. Along the way they preached the good news in many villages of Samaria.
Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip: Go south to the road, the desert road, that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.
So Philip started out, and on his way he met an important Ethiopian official. This man was in charge of all the money for Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
And on his way home was sitting in his chariot reading the Book of Isaiah the prophet.
The Spirit told Philip: Go to that chariot and stay near it.
Then Philip ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading from the prophet Isaiah. Philip asked: Do you understand what you are reading?
He said: How can I understand, unless someone explains it to me? Then he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

The Ethiopian official was reading this exact passage from the holy Scriptures: The soldiers led Him away like a quiet sheep to be slaughtered. Just as a lamb stays silent before shearers, He never opened His mouth!
He was shamed, and justice was taken away from Him. Who can tell about the people who come after Him? Because His life was taken from the earth.
The official asked Philip: Tell me, please, who is the prophet talking about? Is it himself, or someone else?
Then Philip began with that very passage of Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
As they traveled along the road, they came to some water, and the official said: Look, here is water. What can stop me from being baptized?
Philip said: If you believe with all your heart, you may. And he answered: I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the official went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the official did not see him again. But the official went on his way full of joy.
Philip, however, appeared at Azotus and traveled about, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he reached Caesarea.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the persecution and scattering of the Jerusalem church, Philip's ministry in Samaria including the confrontation with Simon the sorcerer, and Philip's encounter with the Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still full of anger and threats to kill the Lord's disciples. He went to the high priest
He asked the high priest for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted permission that if he found any men or women there who followed the Way, he could take them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
As he neared Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
Saul asked: Who are You, Lord? He replied: I am Jesus, the One you are persecuting.
Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.
The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the sound but did not see anyone.
Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could see nothing. So his companions led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he was blind, and did not eat or drink anything.
In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision: Ananias! He answered: Yes, Lord.
The Lord told him: Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.
Ananias answered: Lord, I have heard many reports about this man, and all the harm he has done to Your holy people in Jerusalem.
And he has come here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.
But the Lord said to Ananias: Go! This man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.

Then Ananias went to the house and entered it. He placed his hands on Saul and said: Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me. He appeared to you on the road as you were coming here. He sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Immediately something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,
And after taking some food, he regained his strength. Saul spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.
At once he began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

All those who heard him were amazed and asked: Is this not the man who caused so much trouble in Jerusalem for those who called on this name? Did he not come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?
Yet Saul grew more and more powerful, and he confused the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days had gone by, the Jews made a secret plan to kill him,
But Saul learned of their plan. Day and night they kept close watch on the city gates in order to kill him.
But his followers took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the wall.
When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he really was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on his journey, and that the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how in Damascus, Saul had preached fearlessly in the name of Jesus.
So Saul stayed with them and moved about freely in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
He talked and argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.
When the believers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had a time of peace and grew stronger. The believers lived with respect for the Lord, and the Holy Spirit encouraged them. More and more people joined them.
As Peter traveled about the country, he went to visit the Lord's people who lived in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who could not move and had been lying in bed for eight years.
Peter said to him: Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and roll up your mat. Right away, Aeneas got up.
All those who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, whose name in Greek is Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping the poor.
About that time she became sick and died. Her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa, and the disciples, hearing that Peter was in Lydda, sent two men who urged him: Please come at once!

Peter went with them, and when he arrived, he was taken upstairs to the room. All the widows stood around him, crying. They showed him the robes and other clothes that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
Peter sent them all out of the room. Then he got down on his knees and prayed. Turning toward the dead woman, he said: Tabitha, get up. She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called for the believers, especially the widows, and presented her to them alive.
This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a man named Simon, who made leather for a living.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Saul's dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus, his blindness and healing through Ananias, his escape from Damascus and cautious reception by the apostles in Jerusalem through Barnabas's advocacy, and Peter's healings of Aeneas and Tabitha (Dorcas). All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius. He was an army officer in what was called the Italian Group of soldiers.
He and his whole family were faithful and respected God. He gave generously to those in need, and he prayed to God regularly.
One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said: Cornelius!
Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked: What is it, Lord? The angel answered: Your prayers and your gifts to the poor have gone up to God like an offering He remembers.
Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter.
He is staying with Simon, a man who makes leather for a living, whose house is by the sea.
When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a faithful soldier, one of his personal helpers.
He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.
About noon the following day, as they were on their journey and approaching the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, Peter fell into a deep vision.
He saw heaven opened and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
It contained all kinds of four-footed animals, as well as reptiles and birds.
Then a voice told him: Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.
Peter replied: Surely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything unclean or forbidden.
The voice spoke to him a second time: Do not call anything unclean that God has made clean.
This happened three times, and immediately the sheet was taken back to heaven.
While Peter was wondering about the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found out where Simon's house was and stopped at the gate.
They called out, asking if Simon who was known as Peter was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him: Simon, three men are looking for you.
So get up and go downstairs. Do not be afraid to go with them, because I have sent them.
Peter went down and said to the men: I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?

The men replied: We have come from Cornelius, an army officer. He is a good man who respects God, and all the Jewish people think highly of him. A holy angel told him to bring you to his house, so that he could hear what you have to say.
Then Peter invited the men into the house to be his guests. The next day Peter started out with them, and some of the believers from Joppa went along.
The following day he arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
As Peter entered the house, Cornelius met him and bowed down at his feet to honor him.
But Peter made him get up. He said: Stand up. I am only a man myself.
While talking with him, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people.

He said to them: You know well that it is against our law for a Jewish man to spend time with or visit someone who is not Jewish. But God has shown me something. I should not call anyone unclean or unworthy.
So when you sent for me, I came without arguing. May I ask why you sent for me?
Cornelius answered: Four days ago I was in my house praying at this hour, at three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in shining clothes stood before me
And said: Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and remembered your gifts to the poor.
Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon, who makes leather for a living, and lives by the sea.
So I sent for you immediately, and it was good of you to come. Now we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has commanded you to tell us.
Then Peter began to speak: I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism
But accepts from every nation the one who fears Him and does what is right.
You know the message God sent to the people of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
You know what has happened throughout the province of Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John preached.
God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil. God was with Him.
We are witnesses of everything He did in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed Him by hanging Him on a cross,
But God raised Him from the dead on the third day and let people see Him.
He was not seen by all the people. He was seen by witnesses whom God had already chosen. We are those witnesses. We ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
He commanded us to preach to the people. He told us to say that He is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets speak about Him, saying that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the non-Jewish people.
For they heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said:
Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.
So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Cornelius's vision of an angel, Peter's vision of the sheet with unclean animals, Peter's sermon at Cornelius's household, and the Holy Spirit falling on Gentile believers for the first time -- the pivotal moment where the gospel is confirmed to be for all nations, not Jews only. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: The apostles and the believers all through Judea heard that the non-Jewish people had also received the word of God.
When Peter went up to Jerusalem, the Jewish believers criticized him.
They said: You went into the house of non-Jewish men and ate with them.
Peter began to explain everything to them, just as it had happened:

I was in the city of Joppa praying. I fell into a trance and saw a vision. I saw something like a large sheet coming down from heaven. It was let down by its four corners, and it came down to where I was.
I looked closely and saw animals with four feet, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
Then I heard a voice telling me: Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.
I replied: Never, Lord! I have never eaten anything unclean.
The voice spoke from heaven again: Do not call anything unclean that God has made clean.
This happened three times, and then it was all pulled up to heaven again.
Just then, three men sent to me from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me not to hesitate to go with them. These six brothers went with me too, and we all went into the man's house.
He told us that he had seen an angel standing in his house. The angel said: Send men to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter.
He will bring you a message. Through it, you and everyone in your house will be saved.
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them as He had come on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
God gave them the same gift He gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ. So who was I to think I could stand in God's way?
When they heard this, they stopped objecting and praised God. They said: So then, God has given the non-Jewish people the chance to turn away from sin and live.
Now the believers who had been scattered because of the persecution that started when Stephen was killed had traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They spread the word only among Jews.
But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch. They began to speak to Greeks too, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's power was with them, and many people believed and turned to the Lord.
News of this reached the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When Barnabas arrived and saw what the grace of God had done, he was glad. He encouraged everyone to stay true to the Lord with all their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many more people were brought to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
When he found Saul, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year, Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught many people. The disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.
During this time some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up. Through the Spirit, he predicted that a bad famine would spread over the whole Roman world. This happened while Claudius was emperor.
So the disciples decided that each one would give what he could to help the brothers and sisters living in Judea.
They did this, and sent their gift to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Peter's defense of his visit to Cornelius before the circumcised believers in Jerusalem, the founding of the multi-ethnic church at Antioch (where believers were first called Christians), Barnabas bringing Saul to help lead it, and the prophecy of Agabus prompting famine relief for Judea. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: About this time, King Herod arrested some people who belonged to the church. He wanted to hurt them.
He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish leaders, he also arrested Peter. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting Peter, Herod put him in prison. He handed Peter over to four groups of four soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out for public trial after the Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was praying hard to God for him.
The night before Herod planned to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers. He was bound with two chains, and guards stood watch at the entrance.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and a light shone in the cell. The angel hit Peter on the side to wake him up. He said: Quick, get up! Then the chains fell off Peter's wrists.
Then the angel said to him: Put on your clothes and sandals. Peter did this. The angel said: Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.
Peter followed him out of the prison. But he did not know that what the angel was doing was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate that led to the city. It opened for them by itself, and they walked through it. When they had walked the length of one street, the angel suddenly left him.
Then Peter came to his senses and said: Now I know for certain that the Lord sent His angel. He rescued me from Herod's power and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen to me.
When Peter realized this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John (also called Mark). Many people had gathered there and were praying.
Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door.
When Rhoda recognized Peter's voice, she was so happy that she ran back without opening the door. She said: Peter is at the door!
They said to her: You are out of your mind. But she kept insisting it was true. So they said: It must be his angel.
But Peter kept on knocking. When they opened the door and saw him, they were amazed.
Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet. He told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. He said: Tell James and the other believers about this. Then he left for another place.
In the morning, the soldiers were very upset, wondering what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched everywhere for Peter but could not find him. So he questioned the guards and ordered them to be put to death. Then Herod went from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod had been angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. So they joined together and asked to meet with him. First they won the support of Blastus, a trusted servant of the king. Then they asked for peace, because they depended on the king's country for their food.
On the chosen day, Herod put on his royal robes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to the people.
They shouted: This is the voice of a god, not of a man.
Right away, an angel of the Lord struck Herod down, because he did not give the praise to God. Herod was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God continued to spread and grow.

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers King Herod's persecution of the church including James's martyrdom, Peter's angel-assisted escape from prison, the church's prayer meeting at Mary's house (including Rhoda's excited response at the door), and Herod's sudden death for accepting worship as a god. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard; angels are not capitalized, matching the convention used throughout this site.

verses.text: In the church at Antioch, there were prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon (called Niger), Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had grown up with Herod the ruler), and Saul.
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: Set apart Barnabas and Saul for me. I have called them to do special work.
So after they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.
The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul on their way. They went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
When they arrived at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.
They traveled through the whole island until they came to Paphos. There they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
Bar-Jesus was a close helper of the governor, Sergius Paulus. The governor was a smart man. He sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the sorcerer (that is what his name means) fought against them. He tried to turn the governor away from the faith.
Then Saul, who was also called Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
And said: You are a child of the devil! You are an enemy of everything that is right. You are full of lies and tricks. Will you never stop twisting the right ways of the Lord?

Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind for a while. You will not even be able to see the light of the sun. Right away, mist and darkness came over Elymas. He walked around trying to find someone to lead him by the hand.
When the governor saw what had happened, he believed. He was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.
From Paphos, Paul and his companions sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. There, John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
From Perga they went on to Pisidian Antioch. On the Sabbath they entered the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them. They said: Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said: Fellow Israelites, and you non-Jewish people who worship God, listen to me!
The God of the people of Israel chose our ancestors. He made them do well while they were foreigners in Egypt. Then, with great power, He led them out of that country,
And for about forty years He put up with them in the wilderness.
He defeated seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people to keep.
All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then the people asked for a king. God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin. Saul ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God made David their king. God said about David: I have found David, son of Jesse, a man after my own heart. He will do everything I want him to do.
From this man's descendants God has brought to Israel the Savior He promised, Jesus.
Before Jesus came, John preached that all the people of Israel should turn from sin and be baptized.
As John was finishing his work, he said: Who do you think I am? I am not the one you are looking for. But there is One coming after me. I am not good enough to untie His sandals.
Fellow children of Abraham, and you non-Jewish people who worship God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.
The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus. But by condemning Him, they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
They found no real reason to put Jesus to death, but they still asked Pilate to have Him killed.
When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the cross and laid Him in a tomb.
But God raised Him from the dead,
For many days after that, He was seen by those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.
We tell you the good news: What God promised our ancestors
God has fulfilled this promise for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: You are my Son. Today I have become your father.
God raised Jesus from the dead so that His body would never rot. As God has said: I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.
So it is also said in another place: You will not let Your Holy One see decay.
When David had served God's purpose in his own lifetime, he died. He was buried with his ancestors, and his body decayed.
But the One whom God raised from the dead did not decay.
So, my friends, I want you to know this: through Jesus, the forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
Through Him, everyone who believes is set free from every sin. This is something the law of Moses could never do for you.
Take care that what the prophets have said does not happen to you:
Look, you who mock! Be amazed, and then die, for I am going to do something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people invited them to speak further about these things on the next Sabbath.
When the meeting ended, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas. Paul and Barnabas talked with them and urged them to continue trusting in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
When the Jews saw the crowds, they became jealous. They began to argue against what Paul was saying and insulted him.

Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: We had to speak the word of God to you first. But you reject it. You do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life. So now we turn to the non-Jewish people.
For this is what the Lord has commanded us: I have made you a light for the non-Jewish people. You will bring salvation to the ends of the earth.
When the non-Jewish people heard this, they were glad and honored the word of the Lord. All who were chosen for eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.
But the Jewish leaders stirred up the God-fearing women of high standing and the leading men of the city. They caused trouble for Paul and Barnabas and threw them out of their region.
So they shook the dust off their feet as a warning to them and went to Iconium.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the Holy Spirit's commissioning of Barnabas and Saul at Antioch, the start of the first missionary journey through Cyprus (including the confrontation with Elymas the sorcerer and the first use of the name 'Paul'), and Paul's synagogue sermon at Pisidian Antioch tracing Israel's history to Jesus. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue. They spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the other non-Jewish people. They turned their minds against the brothers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord proved that His message of grace was true by letting them perform signs and wonders.
The people of the city were divided; some sided with the Jews, others with the apostles.
The non-Jewish people and Jews, together with their leaders, made a plan to hurt Paul and Barnabas and stone them.
But they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding country,
Where they kept on preaching the good news.
In Lystra there sat a man who was lame. He had been that way from birth and had never walked.
He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked directly at him, saw that he had faith to be healed,
And called out: Stand up on your feet! At that, the man jumped up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language: The gods have come down to us, looking like humans!
They called Barnabas Zeus, and they called Paul Hermes, because he did most of the talking.
The priest of Zeus had a temple just outside the city. He brought bulls and flowers to the city gates because he and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas.
But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting:

Friends, why are you doing this? We are only human too, just like you. We are bringing you good news. We are telling you to turn away from these worthless things and turn to the living God, who made heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them.
In the past, He let all nations go their own way.
But He has always shown you proof that He is real. He has shown kindness by giving you rain from heaven and crops at the right time. He gives you plenty of food and fills your hearts with joy.
Even after saying all this, Paul and Barnabas could barely stop the crowd from sacrificing to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But after the disciples had gathered around him, Paul got up and went back into the city. The next day, he and Barnabas left for Derbe.
They preached the good news in Derbe and gained many disciples. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
They strengthened the disciples and encouraged them to remain true to the faith. They said: We must go through many hard times to enter the kingdom of God.
Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church. With prayer and fasting, they gave these elders over to the Lord, in whom they had put their trust.
After going through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia,
And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From Attalia, they sailed back to Antioch. This was the place where they had been given over to the grace of God for the work they had now finished.
When they arrived, they gathered the church together. They reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the non-Jewish people.
And they stayed there a long time with the disciples.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Paul and Barnabas's ministry at Iconium and Lystra, including healing a man lame from birth, being mistaken for the gods Zeus and Hermes, Paul's stoning and miraculous recovery, and the return journey appointing elders and strengthening the young churches. All pronouns referring to God are capitalized per this site's standard; the Greek/Roman gods Zeus and Hermes are not capitalized as pronouns since they are not the God of this site's convention.

verses.text: Some men came down from Judea to Antioch. They taught the believers: Unless you are circumcised the way Moses taught, you cannot be saved.

This caused a sharp argument between Paul and Barnabas and these men. So the church chose Paul and Barnabas, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem. They were to talk with the apostles and elders about this question.
The church sent them on their way. As they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the non-Jewish people had turned to God. This news made all the believers very glad.
When they came to Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders welcomed them. Paul and Barnabas reported everything God had done through them.
Then some believers who belonged to the group called the Pharisees stood up and said: The non-Jewish people must be circumcised. They must be required to keep the law of Moses.
The apostles and elders met to consider this question.
After much discussion, Peter stood up and spoke to them: Brothers, you know that some time ago God chose me from among you. Through me, the non-Jewish people heard the good news and believed.
God knows every heart. He showed that He accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He did for us.
He made no difference between us and them. He made their hearts clean through faith.
So now, why do you try to test God? Why put a heavy burden on the non-Jewish disciples that neither we nor our ancestors could carry?
No! We believe it is through the grace of our Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.
The whole group became silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul. Barnabas and Paul told about the signs and wonders God had done among the non-Jewish people through them.
When they finished, James spoke up: Brothers, listen to me.
Simon has told us how God first acted to choose a people for His name from the non-Jewish people.
The words of the prophets are in agreement with this, as it is written:
After this I will return and rebuild David's fallen tent. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
So that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, even all the non-Jewish people who bear my name, says the Lord, who does these things
That have been known for ages.
So it is my judgment that we should not make it hard for the non-Jewish people who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them. We should tell them to stay away from food offered to idols, from sexual sin, from the meat of animals that were strangled, and from blood.
For the law of Moses has been preached in every city from the earliest times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to choose some of their own men and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas (called Barsabbas) and Silas, two leaders among the believers.
With them they sent this letter: From the apostles and elders, your brothers. To the non-Jewish believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
We have heard that some men went out from us without our permission. They troubled you and confused your minds by what they said.
So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul,
Men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we are sending Judas and Silas. They will tell you in person the same things we are writing.
The Holy Spirit and we agreed not to place on you any burden beyond these things:
Stay away from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual sin. You will do well if you avoid these things. Farewell.
So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they gathered the church together and delivered the letter.
The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.
Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the believers.
After spending some time there, the believers sent them back in peace to those who had sent them.
But Silas decided to stay there.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. They and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord.
Some time later Paul said to Barnabas: Let us go back. Let us visit the believers in every town where we preached the word of the Lord. Let us see how they are doing.
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, with them,
But Paul did not think it was wise to take him. John Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had not continued the work with them.
They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
But Paul chose Silas. The believers gave Paul over to the grace of the Lord, and he left.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the Jerusalem Council's pivotal decision that Gentile believers need not be circumcised or keep the full law of Moses, James's citation of the prophets, the letter sent to Antioch, and the sharp split between Paul and Barnabas over John Mark that led to two missionary teams instead of one. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland roads and arrived at Ephesus. There he found some disciples
And asked them: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed? They answered: No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.
So Paul asked: Then what baptism did you receive? They replied: John's baptism.
Paul said: John's baptism was a baptism for turning from sin. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him. That is, in Jesus.
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them. They spoke in other languages and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months. He argued persuasively about the kingdom of God.

But some of them became stubborn and refused to believe. They spoke evil about the Way in front of everyone. So Paul left them and took the disciples with him. He had discussions every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that all the Jews and Greeks who lived in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord.
God did extraordinary miracles through Paul,
Even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul were taken to sick people. Their illnesses were healed, and evil spirits left them.

Some Jews who traveled around driving out evil spirits tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus over people who had demons. They would say: In the name of Jesus, the One Paul preaches about, I command you to come out.
Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
One day the evil spirit answered them: Jesus I know, and Paul I know about, but who are you?
Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
When this became known to the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, they were all filled with fear. The name of the Lord Jesus was greatly honored.
Many of those who believed now came and openly confessed what they had done.

A number of people who had practiced magic brought their scrolls together and burned them in front of everyone. When they added up the value of the scrolls, it came to fifty thousand pieces of silver.
In this way the word of the Lord spread widely and grew in power.
After all this had happened, Paul decided to go to Jerusalem by way of Macedonia and Achaia. He said: I must visit Rome too.
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed in the province of Asia a little longer.
About that time, a great disturbance broke out about the Way.
A silversmith named Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis. He brought in a lot of business for the craftsmen there.
He called them together, along with the workers in related trades, and said: You know, my friends, that we receive a good income from this business.

You have seen and heard how this man Paul has convinced and misled large numbers of people here in Ephesus. It is the same almost everywhere in the province of Asia. He says that gods made by human hands are not real gods at all.

There is danger that our trade will lose its good name. There is also danger that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will lose its honor. Artemis herself is worshiped throughout the province of Asia and the world, and she could lose her greatness.
When they heard this, they were furious and began shouting: Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!
Soon the whole city was in an uproar. The people seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia, and all rushed into the theater together.
Paul wanted to appear before the crowd, but the disciples would not let him.
Even some of the officials of the province, who were friends of Paul, sent him a message begging him not to go into the theater.
The assembly was in confusion: Some were shouting one thing, some another. Most of the people did not even know why they were there.
The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander to the front, and they shouted instructions to him. He motioned for silence so he could explain things to the people.
But when they realized he was a Jew, they all shouted together for about two hours: Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!

The city clerk quieted the crowd and said: Fellow Ephesians, listen. Does not everyone in the world know that Ephesus guards the temple of the great Artemis? Does not everyone know Ephesus guards her image that fell from heaven?
So since these facts cannot be denied, you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
You have brought these men here, even though they have not robbed temples or spoken evil against our goddess.
So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open, and there are governors. They can bring charges there.
